title.narrative: Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative:
(1) The platform for unity in action called the Cameroon Workers Forum (CAWOF) submitted a proposal on social dialogue to the Government of Cameroon in March 2022. In response to the demands of CAWOF, the government took measures to improve the social dialogue situation which includes: • Invitation to the 12 confederations to nominate their representatives (a total of 30) to the Economic, Social and Environmental Council (CESE). This is to relaunch the CESE which has not been functioning for years. • Convening of a tripartite consultation meeting for preliminary discussions on the national minimum wage which has not been revised since 2014. • Appointment of members of the 22nd session of the National social dialogue consultation and monitoring committee (CNCT). • Invitation for proposals from the unions and the employer’s organization for the review of the 1992 labour code.
(2) The unions succeeded with an upward revision of the 2014 national minimum wage through strong tripartite negotiations from 16 June 2022 to 8 March 2023, following the submission of CAWOF’s demands to the Government in March 2022. Decree N° 2023/00338/PM of 21 Mach 2023 on the Guaranteed Minimum Wage was signed in March 2023 fixing the national minimum wage at 41 875 CFA francs for State employees governed by the Labour Code, 45 000 CFA francs for the agricultural-related sectors and 60 000 CFA francs for all others in the private sector. Building the trade unions’ capacity to understand the UN development in 2022 has helped improve the participation of the unions in the UN System. For instance, four representatives of CAWOF are members of the UNDSDCF Result Group 3 on "Effectiveness of policies and performance of public institutions and enjoyment of rights".
(3) Finally, Unions actively participated in the drafting and validation of the 2023-2026 decent work country programme for Cameroon in February 2023. (1) The ILO organised in February 2022, a workshop on trade union internal regulations and management, background documents and instruments for trade union conflict resolutions were prepared by a working group formed to follow up on the implementation of the workshop resolutions.
(2) To address the challenges that hamper good industrial relations and social dialogue in Cameroon, a tripartite workshop was organized by ILO in November 2022 for the social partners and the labour administration. An outcome of the workshop is the adoption of a tripartite action plan that addresses some of the long-standing fundamental workers' issues raised in several trade union proposals to the Government such as: The revision of the labour code, Updating of the bill on trade union activity and the right to strike, the adoption of the criteria for determining trade union representativity and the Capacity building of labour inspectors, staff of the registrar of trade unions as well as employers.
(3) ILO has organized a workshop in June 2022 to build the trade unions’ capacity to understand the UN development system and be able to engage and influence the processes of achieving the SDGs.

description.narrative:
(1) “Le Groupement Intersyndical de Secrétariat Social” (consisted of the “Union Des Syndicats Libre du Cameroun (USLC), Confédération des Syndicats Autonomes du Cameroun (CSAC) and Confédération Syndicale des Travailleurs du Cameroun (CSTC)) has organized informal workers and facilitate their access to social benefits through the signing of a cooperation agreement with the national social security Fund (CNPS) on 12 April 2022 in order to facilitate their affiliation to the national voluntary insurance scheme. Moreover, in March 2022, about 500 traders in Yaoundé market have been sensitised and organized into the union (USLC) and 16 of them trained as focal points to lead the organizing campaigns.
(2) The “Syndicat National Autonome des Ferrailleurs et de la Sauvegarde de l’Ecosytème du Cameroun” (SYNAFSEC) has lobbied the Government, through the Ministry of Mines, Industry and Technological Development, on the registration of the industry’s workers to the national social security fund during a meeting held in April 2022. (1) The ILO provided technical support through the unions in the process of grouping them together into “le Groupement Intersyndical de Secrétariat Social”. From January to April 2022, the ILO technically and financially accompanied trade union activities to mobilize informal workers to access sustainable social protection through the organisations of consultative meetings and the drafting of actions plans.
